mainTopic: Whether a woman may sell property that came to her before marriage, how the משנה differs from תקנת אושא, and what counts as 'known' and 'unknown' property
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. There the חכמים say a betrothed woman's sale is 'void,' which shows the debate with רבן גמליאל was about a sale already made (דיעבד). A second ברייתא, from רבי חנינא בן עקביא, gives a different version: a married woman's husband has rights that a betrothed woman's husband lacks, and she 'sells and gives, and it stands.' The משנה says 'if she sold.' רב זביד fixes that wording, and רב פפא says the two sources are two different reports of רבן גמליאל. רב ושמואל rule that once she marries, the husband takes the property back from the buyers, following a later vote of רבותינו. The גמרא then shows that the משנה differs from תקנת אושא: the משנה gives the husband only the פירות while she lives, while אושא gives him the land itself, even after her death. Next it defines רבי שמעון's 'known' and 'unknown' property, and a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן's view that 'unknown' means property overseas. The amud ends with the start of a story about a woman who wrote her property over to her daughter to keep it from her husband.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the חכמים compare a betrothed woman to a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the earlier question. In it the חכמים argue to רבן גמליאל that a betrothed woman's sale should be void, just like a married woman's sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא. רבי יהודה said: they said before רבן גמליאל, 'Since this one is his wife and that one is his wife, then just as this one's sale is void, so too that one's sale is void!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a ברייתא as a proof for the question it asked just before this. This step sets up the argument; the proof itself comes out in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say a married woman and a betrothed woman are both 'his wife.' So if a married woman's sale of her property is void, a betrothed woman's sale should be void too. Pay attention to the words 'her sale is void.' The proof in step 3 depends on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
It is taught in a ברייתא
Since
Her sale is void

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yehuda said:
They said before Rabban Gamliel:
Since this one is his wife and that one is his wife,
phrases.notes: The first 'this one' is a fully married woman. The second is a woman who is only betrothed (an ארוסה).

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ מִכְרָהּ בָּטֵל, אַף זוֹ מִכְרָהּ בָּטֵל!
phrases.english: just as this one's sale is void, so too this one's sale is void!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question the גמרא asked just before this section, about whether רבן גמליאל was speaking before or after the fact.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the debate with רבן גמליאל is about a sale that already happened (דיעבד).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה, where the חכמים say 'her sale is void.'

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: we are already uneasy about the new property
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל refuses to apply the rule to old property. He is already uncomfortable with the rule about new property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'We are already ashamed about the new property, and now you want to pile the old property on us too?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back against the חכמים' comparison from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'New' property came to her after marriage. There the husband can void her sale, and רבן גמליאל is already uneasy with that rule. He will not stretch it to 'old' property, which came to her before marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: New property: it came to her after marriage
Old property: it came to her before marriage
We are ashamed or uneasy
You roll onto us, meaning you pile an extra burden on us

phrases.english: He said to them:
About the new property we are ashamed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאַתֶּם מְגַלְגְּלִים עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַיְּשָׁנִים?
phrases.english: and yet you roll the old property onto us as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל's reply to the חכמים' argument inside the same ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between old and new property.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule for new property is already hard to accept. It should not be extended to old property.

steps.title: The proof works: the debate was about a sale already done
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'her sale is void,' the גמרא concludes the debate was about after the fact, and it accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that he was speaking about after the fact. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the ברייתא and agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only call a sale 'void' if it already happened. So the whole debate was about a sale already done (דיעבד), not about whether she may sell in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; when said a second time, it means the גמרא agrees
After the fact, once something was already done

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה's ברייתא, the argument was about a sale that already happened (דיעבד).

phrases.english: Learn from this that he was speaking about after the fact.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 1-2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The debate in the ברייתא was about a sale already made (דיעבד).

steps.title: A different version: a married woman is not like a betrothed woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקביא reports a different answer from רבן גמליאל. A married woman's husband has rights that a betrothed woman's husband does not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן עקביא said: רבן גמליאל did not answer the חכמים that way. He answered: 'No! You said this about a married woman, whose husband gets what she finds, her earnings, and the power to annul her vows. Will you say it about a betrothed woman, whose husband gets none of these?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא with a different version of how רבן גמליאל answered the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבן גמליאל does not complain about new and old property. Instead he points to a real difference. A married woman's husband already has many rights over her, so he may also control her property. A betrothed woman's husband has none of these rights, so her sale should stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who gives a different version of the conversation
No! If you said: the formula for pointing out a difference between two cases
A fully married woman
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
Items she finds
Annulling her vows

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא:
phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כָּךְ הֱשִׁיבָן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel did not answer the Sages this way;
rather, this is how he answered them:
No! If you said this about a married woman,
that is because her husband is entitled to what she finds,
and to her earnings, and to annulling her vows.
Will you say the same about a betrothed woman,
whose husband is not entitled to what she finds,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ וְלֹא בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרֶיהָ!
phrases.english: nor to her earnings, nor to annulling her vows?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּךְ הֱשִׁיבָן רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of רבן גמליאל's reply from the one in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothed woman's sale stands, because her husband does not yet have the rights a married woman's husband has.

steps.title: What if she married first and then sold?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים accept the betrothed case. Now they ask about a woman who married first and only then sold her old property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Our teacher, that works if she sold it before she married. But if she married and only afterward sold it, what is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים ask a follow-up question about a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling while still betrothed is now clear. The new question is about a woman who is already fully married when she sells property that came to her before the marriage. At that point her husband has all the rights listed in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Before she was married
What is the law?

phrases.english: They said to him: Our teacher,
if she sold it before she married, fine;
but if she married and afterward sold it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבן גמליאל's distinction in step 4 and moves to a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a woman who is already married sell property that came to her before the marriage?

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: even then she may sell
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that even a married woman may sell her old property, and the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Even this one sells and gives, and it stands.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers the question from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the present tense: 'she sells and gives.' That sounds like she may sell from the start (לכתחילה), not only that a sale already done is valid. This wording causes the problem raised in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: She sells and gives, which sounds like she may do it from the start
It stands; the sale is valid

phrases.english: He said to them:
Even this one sells and gives, and it stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, she may sell and give it, and the sale stands.

steps.title: The חכמים: he acquired her, so he should acquire her property
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue that a husband who acquired the woman should also acquire her property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'Since he acquired the woman, shall he not acquire the property?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge רבן גמליאל's answer from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their reasoning: once the marriage is complete, the husband has gained the wife herself. So it makes sense that he gains rights over her property too. If so, she should not be able to sell it.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired the woman, meaning through marriage
Property

phrases.english: They said to him:
Since he acquired the woman,
shall he not acquire the property?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְזָכָה בָּאִשָּׁה, לֹא יִזְכֶּה בַּנְּכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבן גמליאל's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that a married woman may sell her old property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acquiring the woman should bring with it acquiring her property.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל repeats: don't add the old property to the new
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers with the same line about new and old property, now in רבי חנינא בן עקביא's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'We are already ashamed about the new property, and now you pile the old property on us too?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers the חכמים' challenge from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words appeared in step 2, but here they answer a new challenge. The husband's rights over new property are already hard to explain. Marriage alone is not enough reason to give him old property as well.

phrases.english: He said to them:
About the new property we are ashamed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאַתֶּם מְגַלְגְּלִין עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַיְּשָׁנִים?!
phrases.english: and yet you roll the old property onto us as well?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refusing to extend a rule that is already hard to explain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Acquiring the wife should also give the husband her old property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband's rights over new property are already uncomfortable, so they are not extended to old property.

steps.title: The משנה says 'if she sold,' meaning only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a difficulty. The משנה quotes רבן גמליאל as saying 'if she sold,' which sounds like after the fact only. That clashes with 'she sells' in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: if property came to her before she married and then she married, רבן גמליאל says, 'If she sold or gave it, it stands'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between the ברייתא of רבי חנינא בן עקביא and the משנה. The next steps (10 and 11) give two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 רבן גמליאל said 'she sells and gives,' which sounds like she may sell from the start. The משנה has him say 'if she sold,' which sounds like only after the fact. Both cannot be his exact view, so the גמרא asks how to reconcile them.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in the משנה? This opens a contradiction
If she sold, which sounds like after the fact

steps.confusionAlert: The difference is very small: 'sells' (step 6) versus 'if she sold' (here). The first sounds like permission from the start; the second sounds like after the fact only.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה:
if it came to her before she was married, and then she married,
Rabban Gamliel says:
If she sold or gave it away, it stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to challenge the wording in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording 'she sells and gives,' which suggests permission from the start.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's 'if she sold' suggests רבן גמליאל only upholds a sale already done.

steps.title: רב זביד fixes the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says to read the משנה as 'she sells and gives, and it stands', so it permits selling from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Teach it this way: She may sell and give away, and the sale stands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers the difficulty from step 9 by changing the wording of the משנה. Now it agrees with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that 'if she sold' sounds like the sale is allowed only after the fact. רב זביד reads the משנה as 'she sells', which means she may sell from the start. Now the משנה and the ברייתא say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it this way. This is how the גמרא tells us to read a text differently.
She sells and gives away. She may do this from the start.
And it stands. The deal is valid.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: Teach it as:
She sells and gives, and it stands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by changing the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change in the wording of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows the sale only after the fact, which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read 'she sells', so it also allows the sale from the start.

steps.title: רב פפא: two different reports of רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא keeps the wording. He says the משנה is רבי יהודה's report of רבן גמליאל's view, and the ברייתא is רבי חנינא בן עקביא's report.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is not difficult. This source is רבי יהודה's version of רבן גמליאל's view, and that source is רבי חנינא בן עקביא's version of רבן גמליאל's view.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second answer to the same difficulty. Two different תנאים reported רבן גמליאל's view in two different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not change any words. In רבי יהודה's report, which is our משנה, רבן גמליאל allows the sale only after the fact. In רבי חנינא בן עקביא's report, which is the ברייתא, he allows it even from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer.
This one ... that one. It splits the two sources into two different cases or opinions.
According to the view of. Here it means as he reported that person's view.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: This is Rabbi Yehuda according to Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה, which says 'if she sold'.

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: that is Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya according to Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same קשיא that step 10 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different תנא's report
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources report one single view of רבן גמליאל, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא בן עקביא each reported רבן גמליאל's view differently.

steps.title: Is רבי חנינא בן עקביא siding with בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if רבי חנינא בן עקביא lets her sell from the start, does he follow בית שמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי חנינא בן עקביא follow בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's answer. It says רבי חנינא בן עקביא's version seems to match בית שמאי, and we normally follow בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, for property that came to her while she was betrothed, בית שמאי say she may sell it from the start. בית הלל say she should not sell it, though a sale she already made stands. If רבי חנינא בן עקביא allows the sale from the start, he seems to follow בית שמאי, and that is a problem because the הלכה follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי. In the משנה they say she may sell property that came to her while betrothed, even from the start.
The school of הלל. In the משנה, for property that came to her while betrothed, they uphold her sale only after the fact. The הלכה usually follows them.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya,
is he like Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from רב פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא בן עקביא's version, as רב פפא presented it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Allowing the sale from the start matches בית שמאי, not בית הלל.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל never argued about this
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן עקביא holds that בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue at all about this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining רבי חנינא בן עקביא's view more fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן עקביא is not choosing בית שמאי over בית הלל. In his view, both schools agree that she may sell this property from the start. So he still fits בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means. It explains a statement more fully.
They did not argue.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue
about this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל דָּבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining what the speaker really means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא בן עקביא follows בית שמאי against בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: In his view, both schools agree she may sell, so he does not go against בית הלל.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to 'if she sold' versus 'she sells'. רב זביד changes the wording of the משנה. רב פפא says two תנאים reported רבן גמליאל differently, and in רבי חנינא בן עקביא's report both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the husband takes it back from the buyers
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל rule that whether she inherited before or after betrothal, once she married, the husband can take the property back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ושמואל both say: Whether she inherited property before she was betrothed, or after she was betrothed and then married, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling by רב ושמואל about this same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she sold after she was already married. רב ושמואל say her sale does not hold against the husband, even for property she got before betrothal. That is stricter than both reports of רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them.
Property came to her, usually by inheritance.
The husband takes it back from the buyers.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
Whether property came to her
before she was betrothed,
or property came to her
after she was betrothed, and she married,
phrases.notes: The case is that she sold the property after the wedding.

phrases.english: the husband takes it out of the buyers' hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new אמורא ruling on the same subject.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once she marries, her sale of her old or new property does not hold, and the husband takes it back from the buyers.

steps.title: Whose view do רב and שמואל follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב ושמואל agree with neither רבי יהודה nor רבי חנינא בן עקביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is not like רבי יהודה and not like רבי חנינא בן עקביא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ושמואל. Their ruling seems to have no תנא to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports of רבן גמליאל keep a married woman's sale valid, at least after the fact. רב ושמואל say the husband takes the property back. So they seem to go against every view we know.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? It asks which תנא a ruling follows.

phrases.english: Like whom? Not like Rabbi Yehuda
and not like Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? דְּלֹא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ושמואל's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known reports of רבן גמליאל keep the sale valid, so the ruling has no תנא behind it.

steps.title: They follow רבותינו, who took a vote
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל follow רבותינו, who reconsidered, voted, and ruled that the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow רבותינו. As a ברייתא teaches: רבותינו reconsidered and voted. Whether property came to her before she was betrothed, or after she was betrothed and then married, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב ושמואל do have a source: a later vote by רבותינו, quoted in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says רבותינו reconsidered the question and voted. Their ruling uses the same words as רב ושמואל. So רב ושמואל are following this later ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Our Rabbis. Here it is a group of sages who ruled on this question.
They reconsidered and voted.
As a ברייתא teaches.

phrases.english: They say it like our Rabbis.
As it is taught: Our Rabbis reconsidered and voted:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לָהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְאָרֵס,
phrases.english: Whether it came to her before she was betrothed,
or it came to her after she was betrothed, and she married,
the husband takes it out of the buyers' hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ דְּאָמְרִי כְּרַבּוֹתֵינוּ. דְּתַנְיָא, רַבּוֹתֵינוּ חָזְרוּ וְנִמְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by naming the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ושמואל's ruling has no תנאי support.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow the later vote of רבותינו.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ושמואל follow the vote of רבותינו: once she marries, the husband takes back from the buyers even her old property.

steps.title: Does the משנה already teach the ordinance of אושא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that everyone agrees once she married. It suggests this already teaches תקנת אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'After she married, both these and those agree.' Shall we say that we already learned the ordinance of אושא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line in the משנה and suggests it already teaches a later ordinance. This sets up the next step, which explains that ordinance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that for property she got after marriage, בית שמאי and בית הלל agree the husband takes it back. The גמרא wonders whether this is the same as the rule set in אושא. If it is, why was a new ordinance needed?

keyTerms.meaning: Both these and those agree. Here it means בית שמאי and בית הלל.
Shall we say we already learned it? This suggests a source already teaches a rule.
The ordinance made by the sages in the town of אושא.

phrases.english: After she married, both these and those agree.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, about property that came to her after the wedding.

phrases.english: Shall we say we learned the ordinance of Usha?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁנִּיסֵּת אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ מוֹדִים. לֵימָא תְּנֵינָא לְתַקָּנַת אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on another line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the rule of the משנה the same as תקנת אושא, which would make that ordinance unnecessary?

steps.title: The ordinance made in אושא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reports the ordinance of אושא. If a woman sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive and then died, the husband takes the property back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: In אושא they made this ordinance. If a woman sold her נכסי מלוג during her husband's lifetime and then died, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ordinance of אושא so we can compare it with the משנה. This explains the suggestion made in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ordinance sounds just like the משנה: the husband takes the property back from the buyers. That is why the גמרא suggested the משנה already teaches it. The next step shows that the two rules are actually different.

keyTerms.meaning: They made an ordinance, a rule set by the sages.
Property the wife owns, while the husband gets its produce.
While her husband is alive.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
In Usha they made an ordinance:
A woman who sold some of her melog property
in her husband's lifetime, and she died,
the husband takes it out of the buyers' hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ordinance that the suggestion in step 17 refers to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a woman sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive and then died, the husband takes the property back from the buyers.

steps.title: The משנה covers only produce while she lives; אושא covers the land itself, even after death
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lets the husband collect only the פירות, and only while his wife is alive. תקנת אושא lets him take the land itself, even after she dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about the time she is alive, and only about the produce. The ordinance of אושא is about the land itself, and about after her death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17, which asked whether the משנה already teaches תקנת אושא. It shows that the two teach different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the husband can take only the פירות from the buyer while his wife is alive, and the buyer keeps the land. תקנת אושא goes further: the husband takes the land itself away from the buyers, and he can do so even after she dies, because he inherits her. So אושא added something new.

keyTerms.meaning: During her lifetime
Produce, the yearly crop or income from the property
The land itself, as opposed to its produce
After death
The ordinance passed by the חכמים in the town of אושא

steps.whatToRemember: משנה = only the פירות, only while she is alive. תקנת אושא = the land itself, even after her death.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is about during her lifetime, and about the produce;
phrases.notes: In other words, while she is alive the husband takes only the crops from the buyer, and the buyer keeps the land.

phrases.english: the ordinance of Usha is about the land itself
and about after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question of step 17 by separating the משנה's rule from the ordinance reported in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing scope: the two sources cover different things (produce vs. the land itself, and lifetime vs. after death).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה already teaches what תקנת אושא says, so the ordinance would add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה gives the husband only the פירות during her life; תקנת אושא gives him the land itself, even after her death.

steps.title: What counts as known and unknown property in רבי שמעון's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's distinction in the משנה and asks what 'known' and 'unknown' property means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that רבי שמעון divides between kinds of property. Which property is called 'known,' and which is called 'unknown'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for the meaning of its terms. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that property known to the husband is treated differently from property he did not know about. The משנה never defines these words, so the גמרא asks for a definition.

keyTerms.meaning: Divides, makes a distinction
Known, property the husband knew about
Unknown, property the husband did not know about

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon distinguishes between kinds of property.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: known property is treated one way, and unknown property another way.

phrases.english: Which are the known properties,
and which are the ones that are unknown?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן יְדוּעִין וְאֵלּוּ הֵן שֶׁאֵינָן יְדוּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, moving on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of 'known' and 'unknown' property in רבי שמעון's distinction.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: known means land, unknown means movable items
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא defines known property as land and unknown property as movable items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: 'Known' means land. 'Unknown' means movable items.
steps.whatsHappening: The first אמורא answers the question. He divides the property by type: land or movable items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land cannot be hidden, so the husband knew about it when he married her and was counting on its פירות. Movable items are easy to keep out of sight, so he may not have known about them.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, real estate
Movable property, things that can be carried

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
Known property means land.
Unknown property means movable items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the definition question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference depends on the type of property: land is known, and movable items are unknown.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both types are known; unknown means property she inherited overseas
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says land and movable items both count as known. Unknown property is property that came to her far away, overseas, while she lives here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both land and movable items are known. Unknown property is any case where she lives here and property came to her overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question. For him, what matters is where the property is located, not what kind of property it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. He holds that a husband generally knows about both her land and her movable items. Only property that came to her in a far-off place is something he did not count on when he married her.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those, meaning both kinds
She lives here
Overseas, a far-off country

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two answers. For רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, movable items are 'unknown.' For רבי יוחנן, movable items are 'known,' and only property overseas is 'unknown.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
These and those are both known.
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means the land and the movable items from the previous answer.

phrases.english: And these are the unknown ones:
any case where she lives here
and property came to her overseas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer that disagrees with step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both land and movable items are known. Unknown means property that came to her overseas while she lives here.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses the same words as רבי יוחנן: unknown property is property that came to her overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same thing: Unknown property is any case where she lives here and property came to her overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן word for word. That gives his view the backing of a תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way, introducing a supporting ברייתא
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: 'unknown' property means property that came to her overseas.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
These are the unknown properties:
any case where she lives here
and property came to her overseas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition given in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's definition of unknown property as property that came to her overseas.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same words.

steps.title: A woman writes her property over to her daughter to keep it from her husband
steps.stepSummary: A woman about to marry wanted to keep her property away from her husband, so she wrote it over to her daughter. She then married and was divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain woman who wanted to keep her property away from her husband. She wrote it over to her daughter. She got married and then was divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts telling a story about a real case. It is only setting up the facts here, and the question and the ruling come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman did not really want to give her property away. She wrote it over to her daughter only so that her new husband would not get rights to it. Once she was divorced, that reason was gone, which sets up the coming question about whether the gift still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
She would move it out of reach, hiding property from someone (מַבְרַחַת)
She got married
She was divorced

phrases.english: There was a certain woman
who wanted to move her property out of reach of her husband,
phrases.notes: Her husband-to-be, the man she was about to marry.

phrases.english: so she wrote it over to her daughter.
She got married and was divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דְּבָעֲיָא דְּתַבְרְחִינְהוּ לְנִכְסַהּ מִגַּבְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case story connected to the topic of a woman moving her property out of her husband's reach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The facts are set: she wrote her property to her daughter to keep it from her husband, then married and was divorced.
